Name: Dynamic NPC Outfit Selector
Author: aneirine
Description:
[i][b]Ever wished you could pick what each villager wears? Now you can.
[/b][/i]
This mod exists because I got tired of manually swapping files between folders to get the look I wanted for a season or a festival. I wanted something dynamic instead, something I could just click through in-game. 

[b]RECENT UPDATE: 1.1.0[/b]

Outfits can now depend on the weather and on where a character is, not just the season. Give someone a light coat indoors and a heavy one outdoors while it snows, or a look that only shows up at the beach. Locations added by other mods appear in the list on their own.

Also new: a search box for the NPC list, an F9 hotkey to open the menu, and the menu now opens showing what each character is actually wearing.

Your existing settings carry over untouched.


[color=#ffffff][font=Arial Black][i][b]IMPORTANT:[/b][/i] This mod doesn't add any outfits on its own. It's a picker, not an art pack. It reads whatever's already loaded in your game (from Content Patcher appearance packs, or your own PNGs, see Requirements below) and lets you choose between them.[/font]
[/color]

[font=Arial Black][color=#ffffff]Note:[/color][color=#ff0000] festival [/color][color=#ffffff]and [/color][color=#ff0000]beach[/color][color=#ffffff] outfits sometimes have fewer animation frames than a regular [/color][/font][color=#ffffff][font=Arial Black]seasonal outfit's spritesheet. Forcing one onto a different season can cause visual [/font][/color][font=Arial Black][color=#ffffff]glitches (mismatched or invisible frames) if the source art doesn't have a full set. Use at your own discretion, if something looks off, just switch that slot back to "no override."[/color][/font]


[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50375/50375-1786193306-1627950116.gif[/img]

[size=4][b]Installation instructions[/b][/size]
[color=#D4D4D8]1. Install SMAPI.
2. Install Generic Mod Config Menu. It is required for the menu to be displayed
3. Unzip this mod into your Stardew Valley/Mods folder, so you end up with Mods/Dynamic NPC Outfit Selector/manifest.jso
4. Launch the game through SMAPI. Open the mod's page from the GMCM cog on the title screen or the in-game pause menu[/color]

[size=4][b]Main features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Lists every NPC and every outfit variant currently loaded in your game as a clickable picture, no matter which mod (or mods) it came from. [/color][/*]
[*][color=#d4d4d8]Pick a condition from a dropdown — Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter, Beach, or a specific festival, then check the outfit you want for it. Leave it on the blank "no override" card to let the game (or whatever mod normally handles that NPC) keep deciding on its own.[/color][/*]
[*]Applies live: no restart, no reload, just hit Save and NPCs already in the world update immediately.[/*]
[*]Works with any Content Patcher appearance pack automatically, and also with your own [color=#d4d4d8]loose PNG files if you don't have (or want to make) a Content Patcher pack of your own.[/color][/*]
[/list][size=4][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]SMAPI 4.0.0+[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Generic Mod Config Menu is required; the mod does nothing without it.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Content Patcher — optional, only needed if you want outfits from other authors' appearance packs. Your own local PNGs work without it.[/color][/*]
[*][color=#D4D4D8]Outfits themselves aren't included. You'll need at least one of:[/color]
1. A Content Patcher appearance pack (most "seasonal outfit" mods on Nexus already work this way — just install it normally and its outfits show up here automatically), or
2. Your own PNGs dropped straight into Mods/Dynamic NPC Outfit Selector/assets/Characters/ and assets/Portraits/, named "<NpcName>_<Condition>.png" (e.g. "Haley_Spring.png", "Haley_Beach.png"). Subfolders don't matter; portraits are optional. Full instructions are in assets/README.txt once the mod is installed.[/*]
[/list][b]Known Limitations[/b]
[list]
[*]Only NPCs with proper appearance data show real alternatives. Older mods that just overwrite a texture file directly aren't represented as separate options — there's nothing to list[/*]
[*]"Beach" currently covers Ginger Island's beach resort. The regular Pelican Town beach look is swapped by a different, filename-based method and isn't force-applied by this mod yet[/*]
[*]Some assets may be replaced with default ones in case it doesn't have the required animation in their assets[/*]
[*]Forcing a festival or beach outfit onto a regular season slot (or vice versa) can cause visual glitches: mismatched frames or invisible sprites, if that outfit's spritesheet doesn't have the full set of animation frames a regular season needs. This is a limitation of the source art, not something this mod can fix
[/*]
[/list][heading]How the mod decides which outfit wins[/heading]
[url=https://github.com/aneirine/dynamic-npc-outfit-selector/blob/main/README.md#how-the-mod-decides-which-outfit-wins][/url] The three dropdowns combine into a single key, which is what you'll see in config.json:
[code]Spring                                  just spring
Spring::Weather_Raining                 spring, but only when it's raining
Spring::Where_Indoor                    spring, but only indoors
Spring::Where_Beach                     spring, but only while they're at the beach
Winter::Weather_Snowing::Where_Outdoor  winter, snowing, and outdoors
Weather_Sunny                           any season, as long as it's sunny[/code]
You can set as many of these as you like for the same character, and they can all be true at once. [b]The more specific one wins[/b] — the key with more parts beats the key with fewer. Each key gets a score, and the highest score is the outfit you see. The category sets the tier; the parts after it move you up [b]within[/b] that tier:
